findings.title: Options-object construction silently enables rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: When pLimit receives an options object, destructuring now defaults rejectOnClear to true instead of false.
findings.impact: Code that follows the documented default pLimit({concurrency: 1}) behavior will have clearQueue() reject queued promises with AbortError instead of only discarding the queue, which can surface unexpected rejections in Promise.all or teardown flows.
findings.evidence: index.js:6-8 sets ({concurrency, rejectOnClear = true}); readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document rejectOnClear default false; the focused runtime probe reported optionsDefaultClearOutcome="AbortError" for pLimit({concurrency: 1}).
findings.reproduction_or_test: Create pLimit({concurrency: 1}), enqueue one long task and one pending task, await one microtask, call clearQueue(), then race the pending promise against a short timer. Observed AbortError instead of remaining pending under the documented default.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: The type check is guarded by rejectOnClear truthiness, so values like 0, null, or an empty string skip the typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean' branch.
findings.impact: Invalid option types are accepted at runtime even though the public type contract says rejectOnClear is boolean and invalid values should fail fast.
findings.evidence: index.js:12 checks if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'); index.test-d.ts:29 expects a non-boolean rejectOnClear to be invalid; the focused runtime probe reported rejectOnClearZeroThrows=false while rejectOnClearStringThrows=true.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Call pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}); it returns a limiter instead of throwing TypeError.

findings.title: limit.map drops mapper indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper wrapper only forwards the Array.from index when the original iterable is an Array; Set and iterator inputs receive undefined.
findings.impact: The documented limit.map contract is broken for supported non-array iterables, so mappers that depend on the item index produce wrong results while the existing Set/iterator tests miss it because they ignore the index.
findings.evidence: index.js:107-112 passes iterableIsArray ? index : undefined; readme.md:78-85 and index.d.ts:30-43 say the mapper receives the item value and its index for an iterable; the focused runtime probe reported mapSetIndexes=["a:undefined","b:undefined"] and coverage_sweep mapIterable indexes serialized as null.
findings.reproduction_or_test: await pLimit(2).map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => `${value}:${index}`) returns ['a:undefined', 'b:undefined'] instead of ['a:0', 'b:1'].

findings.title: limitFunction no longer forwards call arguments
findings.cause: limitFunction now returns a zero-argument wrapper and calls function_() without spreading the wrapper's arguments.
findings.impact: The exported helper breaks any limited function that expects parameters, despite the TypeScript declaration and type tests promising (...arguments_) forwarding.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-124 returns () => limit(() => function_()); index.d.ts:133-136 declares (...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>; index.test-d.ts:25-26 expects lf('input') to type-check; the focused runtime probe reported limitFunctionArgResult="<undefined>" for an async identity function called with 'sentinel'.
findings.reproduction_or_test: const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); await limited('sentinel') resolves undefined instead of 'sentinel'.

findings.title: Infinity is rejected as a concurrency limit
findings.cause: validateConcurrency now requires Number.isInteger(concurrency), removing the previous explicit allowance for Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY.
findings.impact: Consumers can no longer opt into an unlimited limiter with Infinity, which was supported by the existing implementation contract and still satisfies the public numeric minimum wording.
findings.evidence: index.js:127-129 rejects non-integers; git show HEAD:index.js:123-125 allowed Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY; readme.md:37-44 documents concurrency as a number with minimum 1; the focused runtime probe reported infinityAccepted=false.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Call pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY); it throws TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up.
